questions.question: A brand drops Liquid themes and builds a React storefront that pulls products and manages carts through Shopify's customer-facing GraphQL API. Which API powers it?
questions.explanation: The Storefront API exposes products, collections, and cart operations for custom (headless) Shopify storefronts.

questions.question: An external shipping app must read and update WooCommerce orders over authenticated HTTP endpoints. Which built-in interface allows this?
questions.explanation: The WooCommerce REST API exposes orders, products, and customers over HTTP so external systems can integrate without touching the database.

questions.question: An Adobe Commerce (Magento) team enables, disables, and overrides independent feature packages — checkout, catalog, CMS — without breaking the core. Which architectural trait makes this possible?
questions.explanation: Magento's modular architecture packages each feature as a self-contained module with declared dependencies and override points, easing scaling and customization.

questions.question: A BigCommerce merchant pushes its catalog to Amazon, eBay, and Facebook and manages all three from one dashboard. Which built-in feature does this?
questions.explanation: BigCommerce's Channel Manager centralizes product feeds and orders across marketplace and social sales channels.

questions.question: Whenever stock changes in the ERP, the storefront must update immediately instead of polling an API every minute. What mechanism pushes the event to the store?
questions.explanation: Webhooks POST event payloads to a registered endpoint the moment they occur, enabling real-time inventory sync.

questions.question: A Shopify Plus merchant wants every order above 10,000 pesos auto-tagged 'VIP' with the customer emailed — no custom app. Which built-in tool does this?
questions.explanation: Shopify Flow (Plus tier) runs trigger-condition-action workflows such as tagging high-value orders and notifying staff.

questions.question: A catalog query filtering 2 million rows by category crawls until the DBA creates a sorted lookup structure on that column. What did she add?
questions.explanation: An index builds a sorted lookup structure so the engine seeks matching rows instead of scanning the whole table.

questions.question: Before handling cards, a platform must pass an audit of 12 requirement groups — encryption, access control, testing — under the card industry's security standard. Which standard?
alternatives: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
questions.explanation: PCI DSS is the card brands' security standard that any entity storing, processing, or transmitting cardholder data must meet.

questions.question: A snack-box store charges 800 pesos on the first of every month without the buyer re-entering card details. Which platform capability powers this?
questions.explanation: Recurring billing stores a payment credential on file and charges it automatically on a schedule, underpinning subscription commerce.

questions.question: A Magento store answers repeat page requests straight from memory, bypassing PHP entirely, via an HTTP reverse-proxy cache sitting in front. Which cache is this?
questions.explanation: Magento supports Varnish as its full-page cache: it stores rendered pages in memory and serves them without hitting PHP or MySQL.

questions.question: A Magento developer must flush the cache, run indexers, and toggle modules from the terminal with a single utility. Which CLI does she run?
questions.explanation: bin/magento is Magento's command-line interface exposing cache:flush, indexer:reindex, module:disable, and hundreds of other commands.

questions.question: Shopify's REST Admin API grants each app a bucket of request credits that refills steadily; emptying it triggers HTTP 429 responses. Which rate-limiting algorithm is this?
questions.explanation: Shopify's leaky bucket lets calls accumulate up to a bucket size and drips capacity back at a fixed rate, smoothing bursts.

questions.question: A WooCommerce developer must fire a Slack alert the moment an order completes by hooking `woocommerce_order_status_completed`. Which hook type runs code on events?
questions.explanation: WordPress actions execute callbacks when events occur; filters, by contrast, intercept and modify data.

questions.question: Magento lets admins add product attributes like 'material' or 'sleeve length' with no schema change, storing them in typed attribute tables. Which data model is this?
questions.explanation: The Entity-Attribute-Value model separates entities, attributes, and values into tables, trading query complexity for schema flexibility.

questions.question: A mall retailer lets web shoppers pay online and collect the parcel at the customer-service counter two hours later. Which fulfillment option is this?
alternatives: buy online pick up in store
questions.explanation: Buy online, pick up in store (BOPIS) merges e-commerce checkout with local-store collection, cutting delivery time and cost.

questions.question: A brand decouples its React storefront from the commerce engine and communicates purely through APIs. What architecture is this?
questions.explanation: Headless commerce separates the presentation layer from backend commerce logic, connected via APIs.

questions.question: A merchant wants a subscription store where the vendor manages hosting, security patches, and updates. Which platform model fits?
questions.explanation: SaaS platforms (e.g., Shopify, BigCommerce) bundle hosting, maintenance, and updates into a subscription.

questions.question: Beyond the monthly plan, a Shopify Basic merchant pays a percentage of each sale when not using Shopify Payments. What is this charge called?
questions.explanation: Third-party payment gateways on lower Shopify tiers incur per-sale transaction fees on top of subscription costs.

questions.question: A store lists products it never stocks; when a customer orders, the supplier ships directly to them. Which fulfillment model is this?
questions.explanation: Dropshipping routes orders to a supplier who ships straight to the customer, so the seller holds no inventory.

questions.question: A seller lists goods on Lazada, gaining its traffic and checkout in exchange for a commission per sale. Which selling model is this?
questions.explanation: Marketplaces aggregate third-party sellers under one platform that handles traffic and transactions for a commission.
